speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: asked the Minister for Manpower what measures will be implemented to alleviate the disruptions to our manpower resources, particularly in sectors such as cleaning and hospitality which will experience higher labour demand in tandem with more visitors entering Singapore under the Vaccinated Travel Lane schemes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Foreign workers accounted for all of the employment decline, with Government support measures cushioning the impact on local workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In 2021, even as parts of the economy recover, border restrictions continue to constrain the supply of foreign workers to meet the pick-up in demand.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: At the same time, some foreign workers who were already in Singapore have returned home.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: All of this had led to increasing tightness in the labour market.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The number of vacancies is especially acute in sectors which rely most on foreign workers, such as construction and manufacturing.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Government has been working closely with companies to support their manpower needs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are also facilitating the safe inflow of new foreign workers to alleviate the manpower crunch.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our priority is to ensure that the risk of COVID-19 importation is well-managed to protect our public health.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: With the progressive easing of border restrictions, it will also help facilitate the normalisation of foreign worker inflow.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Ministry of Health has recently announced the easing of measures for travellers from various countries, including Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Government will continue to monitor the situation closely, we will continue to work with the industry and companies to adjust to the progressive easing of restrictions and the return of demand.
